title: A connected group scheme over a field is irreducible

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: G is geometrically connected, so after reducing to an algebraically closed ground field with rational closed points one may argue on components; the irreducible component Z through the identity is a closed subgroup scheme because Z x_k Z is reduced and irreducible and multiplication factors through Z; if another component Z' existed, choose a quasi-compact open U containing Z and avoiding Z', and set W to the image of Z x_k U -> G; W is open, quasi-compact, and a specialization argument shows any irreducible component meeting W equals a translate Zg contained in W, so W is a proper open and closed subset, contradicting connectedness (source lines 1171-1227)

core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 1172-1179): geometrically connected (04KV) makes irreducibility invariant under field extensions, so work over an algebraically closed field with G Jacobson and rational closed points (0479).
Z is a subgroup scheme (proof lines 1182-1195): the component Z through e (047M) has Z x_k Z reduced and irreducible (035Z, 038F), so m|_{Z x_k Z} factors through Z and Z is a closed subgroup scheme.

Contradiction (proof lines 1197-1227): assuming another component Z' (047M disjointness), choose quasi-compact U containing Z and avoiding Z' (0B7P); W = m(Z x_k U) is open (0B7N); W is closed because any component meeting W is a translate Zg by a rational point and W is stable under Z-multiplication; W cap Z' = empty by the same argument, so W is a proper open and closed subset, contradicting connectedness.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to algebraically closed Jacobson situation (proof lines 1172-1179).
Show the component through the identity is a closed subgroup scheme (proof lines 1182-1195).
Produce the clopen W from a hypothetical second component and contradict connectedness (proof lines 1197-1227).
